subtopics.title: The Balanced Equation Is a Mole Recipe

questions.question: The coefficients of a balanced equation give:
options: A mole ratio — never a mass ratio

questions.question: The three legs of every stoichiometric journey are:
options: Mass to moles; ratio across the equation; moles back to the wanted units
Moles to mass; mass across; mass to moles

questions.question: Grams may never cross the equation directly because:
options: Grams are too small a unit
The coefficients speak moles, and a mole of each substance weighs a different amount
The equation only works for gases

subtopics.title: The Prediction — 42 Grams In, How Much Out

questions.question: The molar mass of MgCO3 (Mg 24, C 12, O 16) is:
42 g of MgCO3 is:
The theoretical yield of MgO (M = 40 g/mol) is:
The conservation-of-mass check for this decomposition reads:
options: 20 g of solid + 22 g of escaped CO2 = 42 g, the starting mass
Mass need not balance when gas escapes

questions.question: Percentage yield is calculated as:
Collecting 17 g against a 20 g prediction gives a yield of:
Which is a genuine physical reason for a yield below 100%?
options: Atoms were destroyed by the heat
The molar mass changed during the reaction
Incomplete decomposition and product lost in transfers

questions.question: A calculated yield of 108% most likely means:
options: The product is wet or contaminated, or the weighing is faulty — never an overachieving reaction
The reaction worked better than expected
The theoretical yield was set too high

subtopics.title: The Full Method, the Classic Traps, and Where This Leads

questions.question: The first step of every stoichiometry problem is:
options: Write and balance the equation — an unbalanced equation poisons every number after it

questions.question: For MgCO3 → MgO, the 1 : 1 mole ratio corresponds to a mass ratio of:
In the molar mass of MgCO3, the three oxygens contribute:
'Maximum mass' and 'at most' in a question are fingerprints of:
options: A theoretical-yield calculation — the ceiling the atoms allow

subtopics.title: A Recipe Promises, in Its Own Units

questions.question: The bread recipe's promise — one batch gives one tray — is written in:
options: Its own counting units, batches and trays — like an equation's moles

questions.question: One mole of MgCO3 and one mole of MgO weigh:
options: The same, because the ratio is 1 : 1
84 g and 40 g — same count, different masses

questions.question: The 'two doors' of the calculation are:
options: The question and the answer sheet
Grams into moles at the entrance; moles back into grams at the exit — each with its own molar mass

questions.question: 42 grams of carbonate at 84 grams per mole is:
Half a batch in, at one tray per batch, delivers:
options: Half a tray — 0,5 mol of MgO, which is 20 g

questions.question: The 'missing' 22 grams of mass:
options: Left as half a mole of carbon dioxide gas — 22 g that changed address, not vanished
Stayed in the crucible as ash

questions.question: If the two product masses of a decomposition refuse to total the starting mass:
options: Atoms were lost — reactions do that
The gas must have weighed nothing
The starting mass was measured in moles
The mistake is in your arithmetic, not in the atoms

questions.question: The 'shelf count' formula for percentage yield is:
options: What you actually got, over what the recipe promised, times one hundred
The promise over the shelf count, times one hundred

questions.question: 17 g collected against a 20 g promise is:
options: An 85 percent yield — respectable school-laboratory baking

questions.question: Which bakery mishap matches 'product lost in transfers'?
options: Rolls stuck to the pan — powder left on the crucible and spatula

questions.question: A yield above one hundred percent means:
options: The theoretical yield was a suggestion
A contaminated tray — wet or impure product on the balance, never an overachieving reaction
